dashboard.description: Runtime dependencies of the HOPE platform. TASK-847: every panel here now reads an IN-CLUSTER target. It previously described Proxmox VMs — Patroni/PgBouncer on 10.10.1.200-202, Redis on .120-121, MinIO on .102, Vault on .130-132 — which the platform no longer talks to; that is the 'Grafana still shows an out-of-cluster database dashboard' symptom, and its cause was the Prometheus scrape config, not this file. Panels with no in-cluster equivalent (Patroni cluster role, replication/cluster lock, both PgBouncer pool panels, Redis evictions) were deleted rather than left permanently empty.

panels.description: Was 'TimescaleDB HA (Patroni) — VMs 500-502'. TASK-847 repointed the `postgres` scrape job at hope-postgres-exporter (base/exporters.yaml). The two Patroni panels that lived here — cluster role per node, replication & cluster lock — were DELETED rather than rewritten: hope-postgres is one StatefulSet replica, so there is no leader election, no second primary and no streaming replica for them to describe. A panel that can only ever say 'No data' reads as a broken dashboard, not as an absent feature.
panels.title: PostgreSQL — hope-postgres (in-cluster, single instance)

panels.description: The replacement for `pg_up`, which postgres_exporter REMOVED in v0.19.0 along with its legacy metric map. `pg_scrape_collector_success` is emitted per collector by the collector framework. Note the two lines answer different questions: `up` says the EXPORTER POD is reachable, collector_success says the DATABASE answered. Exporter up + collector 0 is the interesting case — and when Postgres is unreachable entirely the exporter emits no `pg_` series at all, so the collector line DISAPPEARS rather than dropping to zero (which is why PostgresDown carries an `absent()` clause).
panels.title: Database reachable

panels.description: There is no PgBouncer in-cluster — the gateway, the six Python services, the migration Job and the backup CronJob all connect to hope-postgres-rw directly. So this is real backend pressure, not a pooler being bypassed, and exhausting the ceiling locks out the migration and backup paths as well as the application. Alert: PostgresConnectionsNearMax at 80%.
panels.title: Connections vs max_connections

panels.description: Fraction of block reads served from shared_buffers. A sustained fall usually means the working set has outgrown shared_buffers, or a sequential scan is sweeping the cache. Carried over unchanged from the VM dashboard — pg_stat_database is a cluster-wide catalog, so the expression is identical against one instance.
panels.title: Buffer cache hit ratio

panels.description: Commits and rollbacks per second across every database on the instance. A rollback rate that tracks the commit rate is usually a failing migration or a constraint the application is retrying, not load.
panels.title: Transaction rate

panels.description: Per-database on-disk size. This is the number that decides when the 30-day pgBackRest window stops fitting in hope-minio's 30Gi PVC — base/minio.yaml puts that ceiling at roughly a 10-12 GB cluster, at which point the repository has to move OFF this node (the PVC cannot be grown: local-path has allowVolumeExpansion=false). Watch this against that ceiling, not against the PVC claim.
panels.title: Database size

panels.description: NEWLY POSSIBLE IN TASK-847. `pg_stat_archiver_*` is a default-enabled collector and there was no in-cluster exporter to produce it before, which is why the backup alerts in alert-rules.yaml had to approximate this signal through Kubernetes Job outcomes. `last_archive_age` climbing without bound is the shape of a stalled archive: WAL then accumulates in pg_wal until the disk fills and Postgres refuses writes. Any movement on failed_count is worth reading the pgBackRest log for.
panels.title: WAL archiving (pgBackRest)

panels.description: Was 'Redis — VMs 420-421'. The 'Evictions (data loss)' panel was DELETED: the in-cluster Valkey runs --maxmemory-policy noeviction, under which redis_evicted_keys_total is exported and permanently 0. It is replaced by the saturation view, because under noeviction the failure is REJECTED WRITES at the ceiling, not silent eviction on the way to it.
panels.title: Redis — hope-redis (in-cluster; persistence DISABLED, maxmemory-policy noeviction)

panels.description: The panel that matters most on this tier. maxmemory is 512 MiB and the policy is noeviction, so there is no gradual degradation: everything is fine until 100%, at which point Redis returns OOM on writes and BullMQ enqueues fail at the caller. Persistence is deliberately off under the PHI posture, so there is nothing to replay. Alerts: RedisMemoryNearMax (85%, ticket), RedisMemoryExhausted (98%, page).
panels.title: Memory used vs maxmemory

panels.description: Connected and blocked clients. `blocked_clients` counts connections parked in a blocking call — BRPOP against a BullMQ queue is the normal source here, so a non-zero floor is expected and it is the SHAPE that is informative.
panels.title: Clients

panels.description: Command rate and total key count. Key count trending up without a matching drain rate is a queue backing up, which on a noeviction instance is the path to the memory ceiling in the first panel.
panels.title: Throughput & keyspace

panels.description: Was 'MinIO · Vault · Temporal' against VM 402 and the Proxmox Vault HA cluster. Both now point in-cluster. Note that hope-minio's capacity is a DATABASE concern: its 30Gi local-path PVC is a directory on the same /dev/vdb as the PostgreSQL data directory, and local-path enforces no quota.
panels.title: Object storage & secrets — hope-minio · hope-vault (in-cluster)

panels.description: ⚠️ READ THIS AS A DATABASE PANEL. hope-minio holds the pgBackRest repository, and (since TASK-847) Loki chunks and Tempo blocks too, on a PVC that shares /dev/vdb with the Postgres data directory. local-path enforces no quota, so MinIO can overrun its 30Gi claim and fill the disk under the database. The PVC cannot be grown (allowVolumeExpansion=false), so the response is to cut Loki/Tempo retention or move the repository off the node. Alert: MinIOCapacityLow at 15% free.
panels.title: MinIO capacity

panels.description: hope-minio is SINGLE NODE with one drive — a deliberate ceiling, not a misconfiguration (base/minio.yaml). So 'drives online' is 1 when healthy and any offline drive is the whole store: WAL archiving stops and Loki/Tempo cannot flush. Bucket count should be hope-backups plus the hope-loki-logs and hope-tempo-traces buckets the TASK-847 cutover requires.
panels.title: MinIO drives & buckets

panels.description: hope-vault, the Vault hope-api actually depends on — not the retired Proxmox HA cluster this panel used to show. `vault_core_unsealed` must be 1; it is Shamir-sealed and unsealed by the vault-bootstrap sidecar on every pod start, so a 0 here means the sidecar did not run or the shares are stale. hope-api refuses to start while sealed and PHI field encryption fails CLOSED. Do NOT group this by the `cluster` label — it is empty while sealed and populated once unsealed, so grouping splits the series across the exact transition being watched.
panels.title: Vault seal state & leases

dashboard.title: HOPE — Data-tier Dependencies
